question: does ramapo have a teacher education program? like can i get certified to teach elementary school there
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers a Bachelor of Science in Elementary Education, and its Teacher Education and Certification Program is approved by the New Jersey State Department of Education. [1][6]

To pursue it, you must have a GPA of 3.0 or higher and apply directly through the Teacher Education office; see https://www.ramapo.edu/te/. [6] Declaring Elementary Education as a major does not admit you to the Teacher Education program. Review the catalog for the process to be fully accepted. [12]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/AH-BS-ELED) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/declare-major-minor-certificate/)

question: If I want to teach high school English, do I major in English and also do the education program, or is there a separate secondary ed major? How many credits is the education part?
answer:
For high school English, complete a primary major such as English and apply to the Teacher Education Program for teaching certification. Ramapo says its only education degree is a BS in Elementary Education; the page describes secondary education as a primary major plus the certification program, not a separate secondary education degree. Applicants must have a GPA of at least 3.0 and apply directly through the Teacher Education office. [2]

The page does not state how many credits the education part requires, so I don’t have verified information about that. Contact the Teacher Education office through https://www.ramapo.edu/te/. [2]

Sources: [2](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/faqs/)

question: What courses are required for the psychology major, and is there a specific stats or research methods sequence I have to take in order?
answer:
The Psychology BA (Bachelor of Arts) is in the School of Social Sciences and Social Work; a Psychology Minor is also published. [1]
Required: PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology; PSYC 242 Statistics; PSYC 303 Research Methods in Psychology and PSYC 304 Data Analysis in Psychology. Choose one course in each: Social/Organizational—PSYC 226, 345; Cognition/Perception—202, 209, 227; Developmental—212, 241, 263, 347; Socio-cultural—231, 239, 307, 311, 335, 349; Clinical—314, 321, 357; Brain/Behavior—310, 352, 353, 355; Fieldwork/Independent Research—319, 320, 339, 358, 367, 368, 472; Capstone—430, 431, 432, 433, 434, 436, 437, 438, 439, 440, 450, 451. Also select one additional Psychology course. Career Pathways requirements: PATH 001, PATH 001, and PATH 003. [1]
The requirements list PSYC 242 and require both PSYC 303 and 304, but do not state a prerequisite/order between them. The recommended plan for students admitted to the major in 2026–2027 places PSYC 242 in Second Year, Spring (semester total 16 credits), then PSYC 303 and 304 together in Third Year, Fall (total 16 credits). Other plan semester totals: First Year Fall 16; First Year Spring 16; Second Year Fall 16; Third Year Spring 16; Fourth Year Fall 16; Fourth Year Spring 16. Plan total: 128 credits. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-PSYC)

question: Is there a minor in human development or child psychology? I'm in the elementary ed track and want something related.
answer:
The catalog information provided lists a Psychology Minor, not a separate Human Development or Child Psychology minor. It includes development-focused choices that may fit your interests. [1]

For the Psychology Minor, take PSYC 101, select 3 Psychology courses (only 1 from each category, for a total of 3), and select 1 additional Psychology course. In Category 3: Development, choose at least 1 from PSYC 212 Psychology of Aging, PSYC 241 Developmental Psychology, PSYC 263 Child Psychology, or PSYC 347 Adolescent Psychology. [1]

PSYC 241 is 4 credits and introduces lifespan human development; PSYC 263 is 4 credits and focuses on children, especially infancy and early childhood. Both require PSYC 101 INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY. Neither is individually required; each is a Category 3 choice. [1][2][3]

Psychology Minor: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MN-PSYC. For clarification about whether a separate minor is available, contact the School of Social Sciences and Social Work Office: SSSWOffice@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7625. [1]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MN-PSYC) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC241) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/PSYC263)
